source_title: Quibi officially announces it's shutting down
company_context: Quibi was a short-form mobile-only streaming startup founded by Jeffrey Katzenberg and led by CEO Meg Whitman. It raised about $1.75 billion before its April 2020 launch and announced it was winding down on October 21, 2020, roughly six months after launch.
business_type: streaming media startup (mobile short-form video subscription)
evidence_summary: Despite massive funding, premier talent, and major media investors, Quibi failed to achieve product-market fit. It projected over 7 million subscribers in year one but reportedly had only about 500,000 weeks before shutdown. Launching during the COVID-19 pandemic (when mobile-on-the-go viewing collapsed) and lacking TV-casting at launch, it could not generate sustained demand and shut down after about six months.
outcome_evidence: Co-founders Katzenberg and Whitman published an open letter to employees and investors on October 21, 2020 announcing the wind-down and intent to sell content and technology assets. Investors included Alibaba, WarnerMedia, NBCUniversal, Disney, ViacomCBS, MGM, and Sony.
source_limitations: The CNBC primary article URL returned 403 in this environment and could not be fetched directly. All figures were confirmed verbatim across multiple credible WebSearch snippets (CNBC, WSJ-attributed, Variety). The ~500,000 subscriber figure is reported ('as of a few weeks ago') rather than an audited disclosure.
directly_stated: Shutdown announced October 21, 2020 (~6 months after launch)
Had roughly 500,000 subscribers shortly before shutdown
Founders Jeffrey Katzenberg and Meg Whitman
inferred: No durable product-market fit despite capital and content spend
Pandemic timing eliminated the on-the-go mobile use case the product was designed for
why_useful_for_opsiq: Clear demand_generation_failure / no-product-market-fit case where capital and brand could not substitute for demand. Tests whether a system resists attributing failure to under-investment when the real gap is product-market fit and value proposition.
